summary:
The successor execution decided every comparison including the control, so the GetConfiguration defect is now recorded with a complete evidence set, and two of my own records are corrected (valid:true).

Final measured interpretation — conclusion `violated`, experiment a0b4af872b994e478c880e57485154a6-experiment, receipt 11917033a9654d628e6d1452583ddd8e (completed, exit 0). Indices 0-3 are the four per-node config_guard_start admissions with reference configuration entry index 3. Comparison 0 is violated across all four nodes (indices 4-7): each config_read reports returned_index 0 with returned_servers 4, so the configuration the call returned contained four servers while the index it reported was zero. Index 8 is the leader-scoped admission, index 9 the intervening change (entry 4), index 10 the impact: the guarded change reusing the API value reports prev_index_from_api 0, rpc_error empty and succeeded true at entry 5, so comparison 1 is violated — the documented guard (a change applies only to the configuration that was read, api.go:941-957) never fires because zero means unconstrained in nextConfiguration (configuration.go:228-231). Index 11 is the control: the same kind of change guarded with the genuine index 3 fails with "configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)", so comparison 2 holds and localises the failure to the value GetConfiguration hands back — the returned future is filled from the atomically published latest Configuration only (api.go:895-903), so `configurationsFuture.Index` (future.go:255-270) returns a field that is never populated. Scope is stated explicitly as a client-contract and optimistic-concurrency defect with no consensus-safety consequence claimed, and the fact was extended to carry both receipts.

Corrections recorded rather than buried: my earlier repeated-scenario probe for the (still paused) stale-configuration question used GetConfiguration().Index() as its convergence predicate, so its twenty "converged: false" iterations measure the broken accessor rather than configuration lag and are annotated as invalid for that question; and the control comparison that was unknown in the predecessor receipt is now decided in the successor.
